title: Backup memory device error
shortDescription: EEPROM read/write failure detected on the main board.
fullDescription:
Error C0100 indicates that the Kyocera TASKalfa cannot read from or write to its backup memory (EEPROM) on the main controller board. The device stores machine configuration, counters, and serial number in this memory.

The error typically appears at power-on and prevents the printer from reaching ready state. It can be caused by a corrupt EEPROM, loose connector between the EEPROM board and main PCB, or a failing main controller board.

Resetting the controller may clear a transient fault but persistent occurrence requires EEPROM replacement by a technician with the correct serial-number reprogramming tools.

causes.cause: Corrupted EEPROM data after power surge

symptoms: Error C0100 on display at boot

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Switch the printer off at the main switch, wait 60 seconds, and power back on.

fixSteps.title: Check connections
fixSteps.instruction: If comfortable with service access, a technician should verify the EEPROM board is seated correctly on the main PCB.

fixSteps.title: Replace EEPROM board
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces the EEPROM and reprograms the serial number and counters using Kyocera service software.

whenToCallPro: Always call authorized Kyocera service for C0100; serial number reprogramming is required.

faq.a: A power cycle is worth trying, but persistent C0100 needs a technician.

title: Backup memory data problem
shortDescription: Checksum mismatch detected in EEPROM contents.
fullDescription:
C0110 is raised when the backup memory contents fail their integrity check. The stored counters or settings no longer match the verification checksum, typically due to an aborted write during power loss.

Unlike C0100 (hardware access failure), C0110 is a data-level problem — the chip is readable but the data is inconsistent. In some cases service mode can reinitialize the relevant section.

Successful recovery depends on whether only non-critical data is corrupted or if counter/serial data is affected. The latter usually requires EEPROM replacement.

fixSteps.title: Reboot machine
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, wait 30 seconds, power on.

fixSteps.title: Service mode reinit
fixSteps.instruction: Technician enters service mode and reinitializes backup RAM section.

whenToCallPro: Any time C0110 persists after a reboot.

faq.a: A reinit typically preserves counters but custom settings may need to be re-entered.

title: Machine serial number mismatch
shortDescription: Serial number in main PCB does not match engine PCB.
fullDescription:
C0180 occurs when the serial number stored in the main control board differs from the one stored in the engine board. This typically happens after a board replacement without proper reprogramming.

Kyocera uses cross-verification between boards to prevent mixing parts from different machines. A technician must use Kyocera-Net service software to rewrite the serial number to match.

Without this step the machine will refuse to start and continue to display C0180.

causes.cause: Main board replaced without serial reprogramming
Engine board replaced without serial reprogramming

fixSteps.title: Reprogram serial
fixSteps.instruction: Technician connects Kyocera service software and writes correct serial number to both boards.

whenToCallPro: Always — this requires Kyocera service tooling.

faq.q: Why does this appear after a repair?
faq.a: The technician forgot the serial number reprogramming step.

title: Drum motor error
shortDescription: Drum motor did not reach target rotation speed.
fullDescription:
Error C2101 indicates the drum motor failed to reach its target speed within the expected window, or the encoder feedback is missing. This stops all print operations.

Causes include a seized drum from debris, a failed motor, a wiring harness issue, or a failed drive PCB. In high-volume environments this motor wears out around 600-800k pages.

Inspection involves rotating the drum by hand to check for resistance, then electrical checks of the motor harness, before replacement of the motor unit.

causes.cause: Drive gear jam from paper debris

fixSteps.title: Inspect drum area
fixSteps.instruction: Open front door and remove drum unit; check for shredded paper or debris in drive gears.

fixSteps.title: Test motor
fixSteps.instruction: Technician runs motor test in service mode to confirm failure.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces the drum drive motor assembly.

whenToCallPro: If debris removal does not clear the code.

faq.q: Can I replace the drum motor myself?
faq.a: No, it requires partial disassembly and service mode calibration.

title: Paper feed motor error
shortDescription: The paper feed motor failed to operate correctly.
fullDescription:
C2500 indicates the paper feed motor driving pickup/feed rollers did not reach speed or stalled. It can be triggered by worn pickup rollers, a jammed gear train, or motor failure.

Because the same motor drives multiple trays in many Kyocera models, the error affects all paper sources. Users see printing stop at the start of a job with C2500 on screen.

Check rollers for wear and remove any trapped paper fragments. If mechanical inspection is clean, the motor or driver PCB likely needs replacement.

causes.cause: Jammed paper fragments in feed path

fixSteps.title: Clear paper path
fixSteps.instruction: Open all cassettes and doors and remove any paper or debris from rollers.

fixSteps.title: Inspect rollers
fixSteps.instruction: Check pickup and feed rollers for shine or flat spots; replace if worn.

fixSteps.title: Professional service
fixSteps.instruction: If cleared path does not restore function, a technician replaces the feed motor.

whenToCallPro: After clearing the paper path and replacing rollers fails.

faq.q: Does a power cycle clear C2500?
faq.a: Only if the underlying jam has been removed.

title: Polygon motor error
shortDescription: Laser polygon mirror motor did not reach rated RPM.
fullDescription:
C4000 tells the printer that the polygon mirror inside the laser scanner unit (LSU) did not spin up to operating speed within the allowed timeout.

This is a high-precision component spinning at tens of thousands of RPM. Bearing wear or dust contamination are frequent causes on older machines. An electrical failure in the scanner PCB will also trigger the error.

The fix is almost always replacement of the entire laser scanner unit; the polygon motor is not field-serviceable.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Power off for 2 minutes then power on; may clear a stuck bearing temporarily.

fixSteps.title: LSU replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Technician removes and replaces the laser scanner unit, then realigns.

faq.q: Can dust inside the LSU be cleaned?
faq.a: Field cleaning typically introduces more dust; replacement is recommended.

title: Broken fuser heat lamp
shortDescription: Fuser heater lamp open circuit detected.
fullDescription:
C6000 indicates that the main heat lamp inside the fuser is open-circuit — no current flows when the printer applies power. Kyocera flags this immediately because a non-heating fuser cannot melt toner.

Causes are usually a burned-out halogen lamp or a failed thermistor providing incorrect feedback. A failed triac on the power supply could also be responsible.

Replacement is done as a complete fuser assembly in most Kyocera TASKalfa models.

causes.cause: Failed triac on low voltage PSU

symptoms: Pages cold to the touch if printed

fixSteps.title: Cool and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Allow fuser to cool for 30 minutes, then remove and visually inspect the lamp filament.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces fuser assembly.

faq.q: Is the fuser the same as the drum?
faq.a: No. The fuser melts toner onto paper; the drum transfers it.

title: Fuser thermistor high temperature
fullDescription:
C6020 triggers when the fuser thermistor reports a temperature above the safety limit. The machine shuts down to prevent scorching paper or damaging the fuser sleeve.

This can result from a stuck triac locking the lamp on, a shorted thermistor, or a physical obstruction preventing heat distribution. The error latches and requires service-mode clearing after repair.

Do not attempt to clear C6020 without investigating the cause — continued operation risks fire.
symptoms: C6020 after short period of use
Smell of warm paper before error

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Immediately power the machine off and do not restart until inspected.

fixSteps.title: Professional inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Technician measures thermistor resistance and tests triac.

faq.a: No. Investigate first; resetting without fixing risks damage.

title: Fuser thermistor low temperature
shortDescription: Fuser failed to warm up within timeout.
fullDescription:
C6030 is logged when the fuser thermistor does not see the expected temperature rise after the lamp is energized. Either the lamp is not heating, the thermistor is open-circuit reading low, or mains voltage is insufficient.

On TASKalfa devices, C6030 often follows a brief C6000. Replacing the fuser assembly is usually the fix.

In some locations, repeated failures point to low line voltage; a dedicated circuit may be required for larger MFPs.

fixSteps.title: Check mains
fixSteps.instruction: Verify 220-240V or 110-120V as appropriate with a socket tester.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Technician installs new fuser assembly.

faq.q: Can cold room temperature cause this?
faq.a: Only if below 10C; most failures are hardware.

title: Zero-cross signal error
fullDescription:
The zero-cross signal tells the printer when the AC mains waveform crosses zero, which it uses to time fuser triac firing. C6400 is logged when this signal is missing or distorted.

This often points to the low-voltage power supply (LVPS) rather than the fuser itself. A failing triac or opto-isolator on the PSU is typical.

Replacement of the LVPS generally resolves the error.

fixSteps.title: Bypass UPS
fixSteps.instruction: Plug directly into wall socket to rule out waveform issues.

fixSteps.title: Replace LVPS
fixSteps.instruction: Technician swaps the low-voltage power supply board.

faq.a: A pure sine wave UPS is fine; cheap simulated sine units can cause C6400.

title: Toner motor error (Black)
shortDescription: Black toner supply motor failed to run.
fullDescription:
C7001 is raised when the motor that augers black toner from the supply bottle to the developer unit fails to turn. Kyocera monitors motor current; an overload or open winding trips this code.

Check first that the toner bottle is seated and not caked; hardened toner can lock the auger. If that is clear, the motor itself or the driver circuit is at fault.

The error blocks printing because toner levels cannot be maintained.

causes.cause: Caked or clumped toner in bottle

fixSteps.title: Reseat bottle
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the black toner bottle, shake it 5-6 times, and reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Replace bottle
fixSteps.instruction: If reseating fails, install a fresh genuine Kyocera bottle.

fixSteps.title: Professional repair
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces the auger motor.

whenToCallPro: If a new bottle does not clear the code.

faq.q: Does shaking a new bottle help?
faq.a: Yes, always shake Kyocera TK series bottles before installing.

title: Toner sensor error (Cyan)
shortDescription: Cyan toner level sensor gives invalid reading.
fullDescription:
C7101 is a toner level sensor fault on the cyan channel. The sensor is typically a magnetic or optical device detecting toner flow in the developer. When the signal is stuck or implausible, the code triggers.

Contamination of the sensor with toner dust is a common cause. The sensor can sometimes be cleaned; more often the developer unit is replaced as a service item.

Printing is blocked until the sensor reports valid levels again.
symptoms: Cyan cast on prints before failure

fixSteps.title: Reseat developer
fixSteps.instruction: A technician removes and cleans the cyan developer area.

fixSteps.title: Replace developer
fixSteps.instruction: If cleaning fails, replace the cyan developer unit.

faq.q: Will the same code happen on other colors?
faq.a: Yes — C7102 for magenta, C7103 for yellow.

title: Developer unit mismatch
shortDescription: Installed developer unit is not compatible.
fullDescription:
C7401 is logged when the machine reads the developer unit ID chip and finds it does not match the expected model or region. Common triggers are swapping developer units between TASKalfa models or installing a unit intended for another region.

Kyocera verifies region and model on installation; a mismatch halts operation.

The fix is to install the correct developer unit. Cross-region refills are generally not supported.

fixSteps.title: Check part number
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the part number matches your region and model on the Kyocera compatibility list.

fixSteps.title: Install correct unit
fixSteps.instruction: Replace with genuine Kyocera developer unit for your region.

whenToCallPro: If uncertain which part number applies.

faq.q: Can I use a US developer in Europe?

title: Waste toner full
fullDescription:
C7980 indicates the waste toner box is full and must be replaced. The Kyocera machine tracks consumption electronically and locks when the limit is reached, even if the box appears to have room.

Replace the waste container with a genuine WT series box; aftermarket units rarely carry the correct ID chip.

Do not empty and reinstall the same box — the sensor will re-trigger.
symptoms: C7980 after long run of prints

fixSteps.title: Open waste toner door
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the waste toner compartment, usually behind the front cover.

fixSteps.title: Swap container
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the old box, cap it, and install a new genuine WT-xx container.

faq.q: Can I empty and reuse it?
faq.a: No; the chip counter will still read full.

title: Scanner motor error
shortDescription: Scanner carriage motor did not reach home position.
fullDescription:
C8010 flags a failure in the scanner (flatbed) unit: the carriage did not return to its home sensor within the allowed time. It affects copy and scan functions but print may still work.

A common cause is an object blocking the carriage or a broken drive belt. Motor or home sensor failures are also possible.

Open the top cover and inspect the carriage track; clear any obstructions.

causes.cause: Object on scanner glass blocking carriage

symptoms: C8010 at copy or scan start

fixSteps.title: Clear glass
fixSteps.instruction: Remove any items from the scanner glass and document feeder.

fixSteps.title: Inspect belt
fixSteps.instruction: Technician opens scanner unit and checks belt tension.

whenToCallPro: If clearing the glass does not resolve.

faq.q: Can I still print when C8010 is shown?
faq.a: On most models yes; scan and copy are disabled.

title: DP lift motor error
shortDescription: Document processor paper lift motor fault.
fullDescription:
C8140 indicates the document processor (ADF) paper lift motor failed. The motor raises the stack to the feed level; when it does not reach height, copies cannot start.

Check for paper or staples jamming the lift mechanism. If clear, a technician will evaluate motor and sensor health.

Single-sheet copying from the flatbed still works while the ADF is disabled.

causes.cause: Paper or staple jamming lift tray

fixSteps.title: Remove obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Check the ADF lift tray for paper scraps or staples.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Technician inspects and replaces motor as needed.

whenToCallPro: If the path is clear and the tray still will not lift.

faq.q: Can I use the flatbed instead?

title: Finisher communication error
fullDescription:
C8800 appears when the main controller loses communication with the optional finisher (sorter, stapler, booklet unit). Jobs requiring finishing options cannot be completed.

Loose cables between the printer and finisher are the most frequent cause, often after someone moves the finisher for cleaning. A failed finisher PCB is possible.

Power both units off before reseating cables.

causes.cause: Loose interface cable between printer and finisher

fixSteps.title: Power off both
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off printer and finisher.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cable
fixSteps.instruction: Detach and reinsert the finisher interface cable firmly.

fixSteps.title: Restart and test
fixSteps.instruction: Power on printer first, then finisher.

whenToCallPro: If cable reseat does not clear it.

faq.q: Can I print without the finisher?
faq.a: Yes, via disabling finisher options in the driver.

title: DP communication error
fullDescription:
C9000 is communication loss between the main controller and the Document Processor. Like C8800 for finishers, it is frequently a cable problem.

Inspect the connector between the MFP body and the DP for loose pins or debris. Reseating usually clears it.

Persistent C9000 after a good reseat points to the DP PCB or the main board's DP port.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the MFP.

fixSteps.title: Reseat DP cable
fixSteps.instruction: Lift DP, reseat connector at hinge.

whenToCallPro: If reseating does not clear the fault.

faq.q: Is the DP the same as ADF?
faq.a: Yes — Kyocera uses DP for Document Processor.

title: Network engine communication error
shortDescription: Internal bus to network controller failed.
fullDescription:
C9500 indicates that the main engine cannot communicate with the network sub-system. The printer will still function as a standalone copier, but printing over network and scan-to-email are unavailable.

A firmware update that partially failed, or a failed network PCB, are common causes. A factory reset often clears software-induced instances.

Hardware failures require network controller board replacement.

fixSteps.title: Reflash firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Download latest firmware from Kyocera and reflash via USB.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces network controller board.

faq.a: Yes, standalone copy continues to work.

title: System firmware error
shortDescription: Firmware integrity check failed during boot.
fullDescription:
C9900 is a general firmware integrity error. The boot loader found corrupt sectors or mismatched module versions after a power loss during update.

Recovery mode on Kyocera devices allows reflashing with a matching firmware file via USB. The process takes up to 15 minutes and must not be interrupted.

If recovery mode fails the main board or flash chip is faulty.

fixSteps.title: Reflash firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Put correct firmware file on USB stick and follow Kyocera recovery steps.

fixSteps.title: Replace main board
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces main controller if flash chip is dead.

faq.a: Stored jobs and address book may be erased during reflash.

faq.a: No, Kyocera C-codes lock the machine until manually cleared in service mode.

faq.q: Is C7080 a real toner problem?
faq.a: Sometimes — replacing the toner cartridge often clears the sensor reading.

title: Main Motor Drive Error
fullDescription: Error C5101 indicates the main drive motor is not maintaining the expected RPM — often a stuck gear or failing motor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Gears
fixSteps.instruction: Open access cover and rotate gears by hand.

fixSteps.title: Service Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace motor if gears free.

title: Polygon Motor Error
fullDescription: Error C5210 indicates the laser scanner's polygon mirror motor cannot reach speed.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Try reboot first.

fixSteps.title: Replace Scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Install new laser scanner.

title: Toner Motor Error
fullDescription: Error C7080 indicates the toner replenishment motor is not turning. Could be stuck toner or failed motor.

fixSteps.title: Tap Cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and gently rock cartridge to loosen toner.

fixSteps.title: Service Motor
fixSteps.instruction: If issue persists, motor service.

title: Document Feeder Motor Error
fullDescription: Error C8060 indicates the auto document feeder motor cannot operate. Common causes: paper jam, worn rollers.

fixSteps.title: Clear Jam
fixSteps.instruction: Open ADF and remove paper.

fixSteps.title: Replace ADF Roller
fixSteps.instruction: Install new pickup roller.

whenToCallPro: Motor failure after roller swap: service.

faq.a: Yes — bypass ADF and use platen.

title: Fax Modem Error
fullDescription: Error C8400 indicates the optional fax modem failed initialization. Often a loose card or firmware mismatch.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Modem
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, reseat fax card.

fixSteps.title: Update Firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Apply matching firmware.

title: Engine Firmware Error
fullDescription: Error F010 is an engine firmware fatal error. Reflashing usually resolves it.

fixSteps.title: Reflash Firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Use Kyocera firmware updater via USB.

fixSteps.title: Service Engine
fixSteps.instruction: If reflash fails, engine board service.

whenToCallPro: Firmware reflash is service-grade — call a tech.

title: Controller Memory Error
fullDescription: Error F020 reports a memory check failure on the controller — usually transient. Persistent F020 means board service.

fixSteps.title: Hard Reset
fixSteps.instruction: 5-min unplug.

fixSteps.title: Service Controller
fixSteps.instruction: Call a tech if recurring.

title: Fuser Heater Error
fullDescription: Error C6000 indicates the fuser heater circuit isn't operating, due to thermistor or lamp failure.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Try reboot.

fixSteps.title: Replace Fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Install new fuser unit.

whenToCallPro: Fuser high-voltage work needs a tech.

faq.a: Similar but C6000 is broader category.

title: Color Toner Motor Error
fullDescription: Error C7300 indicates one of the color toner motors is not turning.

fixSteps.title: Tap Cartridges
fixSteps.instruction: Rock color cartridges to loosen toner.

fixSteps.title: Service Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Motor replacement if no improvement.

faq.a: Often yes if only color affected.

title: Sorter / Finisher Error
fullDescription: Error C8030 indicates the optional finisher unit's drive motor failed.

fixSteps.title: Clear Finisher
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, manually move tray to home.

fixSteps.title: Service Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Motor replacement if persistent.

title: MCU Firmware Error
fullDescription: C0030 is MCU firmware fault. Power cycle and firmware update typically resolve.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Off 60s on.

fixSteps.title: Update Firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Latest firmware.

title: Fuser Heater Error
fullDescription: C6000 indicates fuser heater fault. Lamp or thermistor failure.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Off 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Replace Fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Install fuser kit.

title: Zero Cross Signal Error
shortDescription: AC power zero-cross signal not detected.
fullDescription: C6400 means power supply zero-cross detection failed. PSU or wiring fault.

fixSteps.title: Different Outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Try direct wall outlet.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Technician.

title: Document Finisher Error
fullDescription: C8030 means finisher (stapler/sorter) error.

fixSteps.title: Clear Staples
fixSteps.instruction: Remove finisher tray and clear staple jam.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: If gear/motor.

faq.question: Staple jam?
faq.answer: Pull cartridge and clear bent staples.

title: Generic Paper Jam
shortDescription: Paper has jammed in the printer.
fullDescription: J-codes indicate paper jam locations.

fixSteps.title: Locate Jam
fixSteps.instruction: Follow on-screen guide.

fixSteps.title: Remove Paper
fixSteps.instruction: Pull in feed direction.

faq.question: Multiple J-codes?
faq.answer: Each J-XX is location code in service manual.

title: System Software Error
fullDescription: F000 indicates total system software failure requiring firmware reload.

fixSteps.title: Service Mode
fixSteps.instruction: Boot service mode.

fixSteps.title: Reload Firmware
fixSteps.instruction: USB firmware load.

fixSteps.title: Replace HDD
fixSteps.instruction: If HDD bad.

title: Drum Motor Error
fullDescription: C2000 indicates main drum motor not turning at proper speed.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Off and on.

fixSteps.title: Replace Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Service replacement.

title: Toner Low Warning
fullDescription: Toner Low warning prompts ordering replacement.

fixSteps.title: Order Cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: Buy genuine TK-XXX.

fixSteps.title: Replace When Empty
fixSteps.instruction: Install new cartridge.

title: Replace Maintenance Kit
shortDescription: Maintenance kit reached end of life.
fullDescription: Replace MK message means MK rated life is reached. Includes fuser, drum, rollers.

fixSteps.title: Order Kit
fixSteps.instruction: Buy MK-XXX matching model.

fixSteps.title: Replace Components
fixSteps.instruction: Install fuser, drum, rollers per manual.

fixSteps.title: Reset Counter
fixSteps.instruction: Service menu reset.

title: Out of Paper
fullDescription: Add Paper indicates tray has no paper.

fixSteps.title: Add Paper
fixSteps.instruction: Open tray and add paper.

fixSteps.title: Adjust Guides
fixSteps.instruction: Set guides to size.

title: C0040
fullDescription: Engine PWB. Common Kyocera printer error. Resolve following service procedure.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 60 seconds, restore.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect cartridge/cable/jam area.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: If persists, service required.
